why:
issue 2015 (2026-10-24) -- PRESENT, as a porting handle. rclcpp splits a node into ~10 `node_interfaces::Node*Interface` slices so a separate package (rclcpp_action, rclcpp_components) can take the part it needs. Ours has no slices -- a node is one object and our components are declared, not constructed with an injected node (RFC-0044) -- so `get_node_base_interface` / `_clock_` / `_graph_` / `_logging_` / `_waitables_` each return a non-owning `rclcpp::node_interfaces::NodeInterfaceHandle` naming THIS node, whose only use is to be passed to `rclcpp_action::create_server` / `create_client`. That keeps the stock `create_server<A>(this->get_node_base_interface(), ...)` call compiling as written. ADOPT-BOUNDED: the handle has NONE of upstream's interface members (calling one is a compile error), `SharedPtr` is the handle itself (no allocator), and the parameters / services / timers / time-source / topics slices are not provided.

EARLIER ROW (declined): the split exists to make rclcpp_components and rclcpp_action composable; nothing to inject a slice of.
